title: Short TESS window phases do not give a robust test of dip deformation in 126 selected CPVs
abstract: We test whether released short-window models of complex periodic variables resolve changes in relative harmonic phases. We use 10,870 TESS windows from 126 stars and an exact interval test that permits any common phase shift and signed harmonic amplitude changes. At separations of 3 to 10 rotations, 16 of 2,572 informative pairs from four stars fail at the source coefficient error scale. At twice that error, none of 965 pairs from 45 stars fails. This does not establish stability. Synthetic independent one-radian phase changes are detected in only 44 of 300 selected pairs at the source scale and 20 of 300 at twice that scale. No pair rejects at four times the error, but that setting also detects none of the tested phase changes. Short-window phase summaries therefore do not provide a robust measurement of general deformation on this timescale. Unknown real covariance, a broad null and sample selection limit the test. We measure no material lifetime or common motion. Code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and repeat steps are included.

display.caption: Short-window phase incompatibility and conditional sensitivity. Zero observed rejections do not establish phase stability. Error multipliers are assumptions.

citations.reason: Uses its verified short-window coefficients and visit periods; audits their ability to measure phase deformation.
Adapts its exact signed-transfer phase interval algorithm to within-visit windows.
Motivates a direct phase test after amplitude changes were shown to move minima.
